claim.why_it_matters: In the PDF, 'FORMAT 4' at the foot of printed page 436 is an ordinary body-weight paragraph label, typographically identical to 'FORMAT 1' / 'FORMAT 2' / 'FORMAT 3' (which the transcription correctly renders as plain text on pages 464, 465, 472, 474 and 475). Promoting it to an H2 injects a spurious document-structure heading at exactly the same level as the '## Page N' navigational scaffolding, so any heading-driven TOC, outline or section-extraction over ISO_COBOL.md gains a bogus 'FORMAT 4' section and the true clause boundary is mis-anchored. It is also internally inconsistent: only 8 of the ~200 'FORMAT n' labels in the file are promoted this way.

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED as a content discrepancy; the underlying typographic observation is accurate but it is formatting-only, which the verification criteria explicitly exclude.

What I independently verified, at 300 dpi and again at ~2x crop magnification of the region:
(1) PDF glyphs. The label 'FORMAT 4' near the foot of printed page 436 (PDF page 466) is set in the same regular-weight serif body face, at the same point size, as the body text immediately above it ('...LINE clause, General rule 4c.)') and immediately below it ('14) Format 4 defines a dynamic-capacity table...'). It carries no bold, no size increase, no small-caps, no numbering. For a control I cropped the running header 'ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' at the top of the same page, which is visibly and unambiguously bold and heavier. So the claim's core typographic assertion is correct: the PDF gives 'FORMAT 4' no heading typography whatsoever.
(2) Markdown. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 19800 is literally '## FORMAT 4'. Both sources are quoted accurately by the claim.
(3) The internal-inconsistency sub-claim also checks out. Across the whole file there are exactly 8 heading-promoted 'FORMAT n' labels versus 192 rendered as plain line-initial text. Within this very clause (13.18.38 OCCURS clause, general rules) the sibling labels at lines 19621 FORMAT 1, 19649 FORMAT 2, 19659 FORMAT 3, 19684 FORMAT 4, 19724 FORMAT 1, 19740 FORMAT 2, 19764 FORMAT 3 are all plain text, and only the run's final FORMAT 4 at 19800 is promoted.

Why this is nevertheless not a reportable discrepancy:
- Nothing is missing, altered, reordered, truncated or made ambiguous. The exact string 'FORMAT 4' is present, in the correct position, between GR 13 and GR 14, precisely as printed. The delta is two '#' characters and a space of markdown markup - i.e. formatting, which the rejection criteria name directly.
- Meaning is unchanged. Any reader, and any consumer extracting COBOL semantics from the prose, receives an identical statement: the label FORMAT 4 introducing general rule 14 about dynamic-capacity tables. No normative content, no general rule, no cross-reference (8.5.1.9) and no syntax is affected.
- The stated downstream harm is overstated because it is not specific to this line. The transcription's heading layer is already wholly non-semantic page furniture: '## Page 466' page markers throughout, and the running header transcribed inconsistently as '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' on this page (line 19778) but '## ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' two pages earlier (line 19635). Any outline or TOC extractor over this file must already filter page markers and running headers; '## FORMAT 4' is one more member of that same pre-existing markup-noise class, not a new failure mode. The genuine clause anchors bracketing this text - '### 13.18.38.4 General rules' at 19701 and '## 13.18.39 PAGE clause' at 19829 - are both present, correctly worded and correctly placed, so no true clause boundary is lost.

Secondary note on the report itself: the kind label 'missing-heading' is inverted. Nothing is missing here; a heading is spuriously ADDED by the transcription. If this class is ever swept it should be filed as an extra/spurious-heading style normalization, not a missing-heading defect.

Verdict: real=false. Formatting-only, zero content loss, zero semantic change. Correctly self-graded 'cosmetic' by the reporter; cosmetic markup asymmetry is below the bar for a reconciliation-ledger discrepancy. If the owner ever wants a stylistic normalization pass over the transcription, the facts recorded above (8 promoted vs 192 plain; the four promoted sites at lines 6280/6284/6288/6298, 19800, 25360, 28029/28033) are sufficient to drive it without re-rendering any page.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The PDF's 'FORMAT 4' on printed page 436 is confirmed plain body-weight text (verified against the bold running header as a control), and specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 19800 does render it as '## FORMAT 4'. However the difference is purely markdown heading markup: the text itself is present, verbatim and correctly positioned, and no normative meaning changes. It is additionally mislabeled - this is a spuriously ADDED heading, not a 'missing-heading'. Downgrade to a non-defect / optional style-normalization note covering all 8 heading-promoted 'FORMAT n' labels (lines 6280, 6284, 6288, 6298, 19800, 25360, 28029, 28033) against the 192 rendered as plain text.
